newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize, wheat futures dip on Budapest grain market.
newsitem.headline: Maize, wheat futures dip on Budapest grain market.

text.p: Maize futures bucked recent trends and dipped on the grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), dealers said on Wednesday.
"There was an inverse market in maize for March, May and July," said Gabor Herczeg of La Salle. "There were signs of a collapse as prices went limit down for March and May."
Maize for the March delivery closed at 19,190, down 320, while the May delivery ended at 18,650, down 350, and July fell 300 to 18,600. Only December 1997 rose, by 200.
Milling wheat prices showed a similar pattern, falling for all maturities except July.
Turnover was a moderately large 411.3 million forints, or 1,037 lots.
"It was not a surprise that maize fell," said Robert Vajo of Termin Brokers. "We have a one-million-tonne surplus while export possibilites are weak."
He said an added pressure to sell in the second half of the winter was that farmers were saving their cash for spring field work and were trying to secure futures contracts to raise money.
He said that prices of milling wheat would have fallen further but for rumours that Serbs and Bosnians were about to buy on the Hungarian market.
"It hasn't really materialised so there's still some selling pressure," he said.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
